synopsis: Continuous automated regression turns captured or synthesised scenarios into permanent tests that catch software-change failures, but neither automation nor millions of runs establishes that the test set represents the real operating domain [f1031, f1032, f671]. Regression must remain separate from failure-seeking discovery and frozen, pre-registered performance estimation; discovered failures should become permanent regression tests rather than estimation data [f133, f6665, f6946, f6949, f7137]. Simulation is intended to select informative physical tests and provide broad regression around physical anchors, with SIL supporting high-volume closed-loop testing, recorded-data replay supporting perception regression, and sensor stimulation supporting final sensor/ECU regression and timing tests [f484, f5266, f918, f4500]. For a team starting from zero in October 2026, an executable SIL framework with dynamics and braking models, continuous regression and fault injection is considered realistic by mid-2027 if software interfaces can be defined; the reported under-a-day incremental validation precedent is a vendor claim for on-road Level 3 assistance [f840, f1307]. Reproducibility and change control require configuration/version traceability, frozen generation inputs, regression testing of simulator upgrades, and physical re-correlation after prototype changes [f5106, f13167, f8897, f11029]. Post-launch perception or braking updates need defined regression and revalidation rules, otherwise 2027 evidence could certify an obsolete configuration; an off-road case addressing post-release software and model updates was not found [f11251, f11252, f11254].
